about: Astoria's people (culture pack C1): one profile per Astoria place, every name invented. A profile whose 'regular' names someone in lib/cast.ts stands at that place in the game; their catchphrases join their everyday lines (content/cast-lines.json) when tapped. Profiles marked 'story' belong to a story's place and only speak through that story. Voice rules: docs/culture/VOICE.md. Edit freely; npm test checks the shape. 'roommates' are the people who share a home with the player (C3): they introduce themselves once and leave a note a day.

template.id: Short id, the same as the regular's id in lib/cast.ts when they stand at the place
template.name: Invented full name
template.background: Cultural background, in the person's own terms. Vary it within a building type; never a punchline
template.catchphrases: Two to five lines they actually say (240 characters or fewer each). No phonetic accent spelling
template.role: Their job or part at the place
template.regular: The lib/cast.ts regular id, or null when they don't stand on the place card
template.slang: Ids from content/culture/slang.json they reach for. Empty is fine: not everyone uses slang
template.story: Optional: the story whose place this is (they only speak through that story)
template.remembers: Optional: { days, line }. After that many different days at the place, their first line is this one (C2: Sal remembers your order)
template.reputation: Optional (Moral Choices, migration 0131): {halo, hustler} lines for players at the 😇 Halo end (70+) or the 💸 Hustler end (30 or below). Neither end is the bad one; never name the meter.

profiles.name: Salah "Sal" Mansour
profiles.background: Egyptian-American, grew up in Alexandria, moved to Steinway Street at 19
profiles.personality: Dry, generous, pretends not to care and remembers everything. Owns the corner and runs it like a small country.
catchphrases: Ock! The usual? Salt, pepper, ketchup. I know, I know.
Also Sal is sleeping on the bread. Take the roll from the other side.
Mira, twenty-two years on this corner. I've seen landlords come and go. Mostly come.
Election's coming. Every campaign wants my bodega in their ad. Also Sal has endorsed nobody. Also Sal is sleeping.
dislikes: People who pet the cat without buying anything

remembers.line: Ock! BEC, salt, pepper, ketchup. Already on the grill. Also Sal saved you a spot on the bread.

halo: You, I trust. Watch the register a second, I gotta find the good mustard.
People say good things about you on this block. Don't make me regret the extra cheese.
hustler: You again. Cash only, and I'm counting it twice. With love.
Whatever you're selling, my nephew already bought two. What do you want on the roll?

profiles.name: Joana "Jojo" Ribeiro
profiles.background: Brazilian-American, born in Minas Gerais, raised on 36th Avenue
profiles.personality: Nosy, quick, spells every name wrong on purpose. Saving for film school one tip jar at a time.
catchphrases: Regular coffee? Milk, two sugars, one rumor. Coming right up.
Deadass, I heard it before it happened.
Tip jar's for film school. Gossip's free with a large.
Four people running against Papa-Dani and every one of them wants a latte on camera. Tip jar's right there.

halo: I spelled your name right today. That's how you know you're in good standing.
Everybody in here says you're one of the good ones. Annoying, honestly. Want a free shot of oat?
hustler: I wrote 'Boss' on your cup. Don't make it weird. Don't touch the tip jar either.
Half the café owes you a favor and the other half owes you money. How?

profiles.name: Efthymia "Effie" Lambrou
profiles.background: Greek-American, born in Astoria to parents from Crete
profiles.personality: Calls everyone hon, hears everything, repeats only the true parts. Has worked the counter longer than the pie case has rotated.
catchphrases: Sit anywhere, hon. Not there. There.
Coffee's bottomless. My patience isn't.
I don't gossip. I just remember out loud.
Some campaign manager sat in booth four for three hours and ordered one coffee. Politics.

profiles.name: Pastor Gideon Vale
profiles.background: Midwestern transplant, came to Queens from Ohio for a radio job
profiles.personality: Smooth, warm on camera, vanity dressed as humility (docs/04-who-killed-sarah-bird-v2.md is canon).
catchphrases: Blessed and booked, friends.
The Lord provides. The building fund helps.

profiles.name: Dr. Eleni Markou
profiles.background: Greek-American, born on 23rd Avenue, first doctor in her family
profiles.personality: Brisk, funny, unshockable. Runs the ER like a diner rush and tells you exactly how long the wait is.
catchphrases: Deadass, drink some water. That's the whole prescription.
The wait is two hours. I said what I said.
Sickness doesn't care about your follower count. Neither do I. Sit.

profiles.name: Marcos Albuquerque
profiles.background: Brazilian, from Recife; came for a gig in 2009 and stayed
profiles.personality: Laid-back jazz bassist who bought the lounge with his bandmates. Keeps the celebrities' secrets and the vinyl in order.
catchphrases: Booth two is taken. By whom? Nobody. Officially.
Bossa nova on Tuesdays. Say less.
Celebrities come here to be left alone. Loudly. I just turn the record up.
dislikes: Requests for songs he's never heard

profiles.name: Lola Lowdown
profiles.background: Queens born and raised; she never says where her family's from, on purpose ("I'm from everywhere you can't get a table")
profiles.personality: Queens' most reliable unreliable source and the city's tea queen: warm, dramatic, always heard something, always on the player's side.
catchphrases: Say less, babe. I already know.
Allegedly. With receipts.
Mad people asked who you are today. I told them to wait.

profiles.name: Camila Restrepo
profiles.background: Colombian-American, born in Medellín, raised in Jackson Heights
profiles.personality: Store manager with a recipe channel and opinions about every shopper's cart. Fiercely practical, secretly sentimental.
catchphrases: Forty kinds of feta. Mira, I've tasted all of them.
Meal prep is cheaper than eating out. I'm not judging. I'm calculating.
Cart's wobbly? They all wobble. It's character.

profiles.name: Valentina Ospina
profiles.background: Colombian-American, born in Cali, came to Queens at 12
profiles.personality: Founder of a scheduling app that, unusually, works. Runs the coworking space's gigs board and has no patience for "between rounds."
catchphrases: The gigs board refreshes every morning. Bet.
Ignore the kombucha. Take the gig.
My app works. That's my whole pitch. Investors find it confusing.
profiles.role: the founder who runs the gigs board

profiles.name: Mr. Desmond Penwright
profiles.background: Trinidadian-born, came to Queens in 1978
profiles.personality: Gentle, precise, a whisperer of gossip and late-fee forgiveness. Has read everything; admits to nothing.
catchphrases: Shh. Unless it's gossip. Then whisper.
A late book is a story that wanted more time.
Your excuse is not new. It is, however, well told.

profiles.name: Sgt. Bev Kowalski
profiles.background: Polish-American, grew up in Greenpoint, moved to Astoria for the commute
profiles.personality: Tired, funny, tells Lola everything. Keeps the precinct ambient: parking reports, lost cats, passionate neighbors.
catchphrases: Another parking report? Get on line, hon.
You're buggin'. It's a parking spot, not a crime scene.
I write it down. That's the service.
dislikes: People who say "do you know who I am"

profiles.name: Captain Rosa Díaz-Moore
profiles.background: Puerto Rican and Irish-American, from Woodside
profiles.personality: Big laugh, bigger heart. Runs Engine 7 and its very late dalmatian, Hydrant.
catchphrases: Hydrant ate a helmet again. Don't tell the chief.
Wepa! Somebody finally fixed the hydrant on 31st.
Pet the dog, sign the calendar, go home happy.

profiles.name: Rev. Mercy Adeyemi
profiles.background: Nigerian-American, from Lagos by way of Flatbush
profiles.personality: Warm, frank, runs an open-door chapel and the best bake sale in Queens. Everyone's welcome, the folding chairs included.
catchphrases: Everyone's welcome. The chairs are a test of faith.
Need ten quiet minutes? Say less.
Bake sale Saturday. The jollof sells out by noon.

profiles.name: Konstantinos "Gus" Pappas
profiles.background: Greek, from Kalamata, came to Astoria in 1968
profiles.personality: Retired tailor, same bench every day, stories about 1987 for anyone who sits. Rates the joggers' form out loud.
catchphrases: Seen a lot from this bench. Want to hear about 1987?
The bridge was here first. Then me. Then the joggers.
Sit, sit. The bench is free. The stories cost nothing either.
Papa-Dani fixed this bench himself. Well, he held the ribbon. Still voting for somebody, though. Haven't decided who.

halo: In 1987 a man returned my umbrella. You remind me of him. Good posture too.
Sit, sit. The bench saves a spot for good people.
hustler: In 1987 I knew a fella like you. Sold me a watch. It was a drawing of a watch. Great salesman.
Sit. Tell me your angle. At my age, a good angle is entertainment.

profiles.name: Yesenia Ortiz
profiles.background: Dominican-American, born in Santiago, raised in Corona
profiles.personality: The station agent who has seen everything twice. Knows when the train is really coming and won't tell you if you're rude.
catchphrases: ¿Qué lo que? The train is two stops away. It's always two stops away.
It's a schlep to Flushing. Bring a snack.
Showtime kids got on at Queensboro Plaza. Hold your coffee.

profiles.name: Sharm Almight
profiles.background: Haitian-American, raised in Queens Village
profiles.personality: Hype, warm, never mean; the voice of The Wake-Up Call on Real Clout FM.
catchphrases: Yo, good morning Astoria! If you ain't up yet, you buggin', son.
Send it in, then pray to the nine o'clock gods. Bet.
likes: Shoutouts that make his mom laugh

profiles.name: Nour El-Sayed
profiles.background: Egyptian-American, born in Cairo, raised on Steinway Street
profiles.personality: Runs the Big Screen's control room. Calm under pressure, merciless with a bad crop.
catchphrases: Three hours on the Big Screen. Make the photo count.
Crop it to the shoulders. Trust me, I've seen thousands.
The whole city looks up at that screen. Odee pressure, honestly.

profiles.name: Arben Krasniqi
profiles.background: Albanian-American, born in Pristina, raised in the Bronx
profiles.personality: Fast hands, slow smile. Has folded a hundred thousand slices and still argues the price is a dollar, spiritually.
catchphrases: Two slices and a soda? Say less. Already in the oven.
The sign says a dollar. The sign is sentimental.
Fold it down the middle. Like a local. There you go.
A candidate ate a slice with a fork in here. On camera. I'm still recovering.

profiles.name: Tariq Hossain
profiles.background: Bangladeshi-American, from Sylhet, came to Queens at 16
profiles.personality: Night owl, philosopher of sauces. Knows every bartender, cabbie and nurse who gets off shift after midnight.
catchphrases: White sauce, yes. Red sauce, careful. I'm not responsible after that.
Three a.m. is my rush hour. Everybody's honest at three a.m.
You look tired, B. Extra rice. On the house this once.
Parking by my cart on a Friday night? Fuhgeddaboudit.
The billionaire's driver comes by at two a.m. White sauce, no red. Even his driver has a strategy.
likes: Regulars who say his name right
Cold nights with a long line
dislikes: People who ask for the sauce on the side

profiles.name: Luisa "Lou" Ferraro
profiles.background: Italian-American, born in Bensonhurst, Astoria by marriage
profiles.personality: Loud, kind, gives directions nobody asked for. Thirty summers at the park gate and a hot dog for every lost tourist.
catchphrases: Onions? Mustard? Don't ask about the water. Nobody asks about the water.
You drove to the park? Next time take the train. I'm right by the stop.
Mad hot out. Get two. One for the walk.

profiles.name: Andreas Charalambous
profiles.background: Greek Cypriot, from Limassol, came to Astoria in 1994
profiles.personality: Host first, chef second, shouter of 'Opa!' third. Remembers every name day on 30th Avenue.
catchphrases: Opa! Sit, sit. The bread is coming whether you want it or not.
Today is somebody's name day. It's always somebody's name day.
The octopus? Facts. Best in Queens. Don't tell my cousin.
dislikes: Empty plates going back half full

profiles.name: Herschel "Hersh" Weiss
profiles.background: Jewish New Yorker, grew up in Crown Heights, opened the deli in 1989
profiles.personality: Gruff at the counter, generous in the kitchen. Slices pastrami by hand, gives free pickles to anyone who looks hungry.
catchphrases: On line, not in line. You're in New York now.
You want a schmear? Everything bagel, schmear, done. Next.
Don't kvetch about the wait. Kvetch about the rent. The wait is worth it.
The professor came in, ordered an everything bagel, and explained the 7 train to the whole line. Twenty minutes. Nobody left. Respect.

profiles.name: Akosua "Kiki" Mensah
profiles.background: Ghanaian-American, born in Kumasi, raised in the Bronx
profiles.personality: Runs the rooftop's guest list like a border crossing and the party like a family reunion. Roots for the Bronx Bigshots in a Queens bar, loudly, on purpose.
catchphrases: You on the list? You're on the list. Don't tell anyone how easy that was.
Best view of the skyline in Queens. Deadass. Ask anybody who's been to the other ones.
New Year's up here: heaters, a countdown and nobody wearing a diaper. Times Square could never.
Kaylee Starr filmed a whole campaign video on this roof. Six hours. Forty seconds of video. Deadass.
dislikes: Meteors fans gloating (rare, to be fair)

profiles.name: Teodoro "Teddy" Bautista
profiles.background: Filipino-American, born in Manila, raised in Woodside
profiles.personality: The building's super for twenty-two years. Fixes everything, forgets nothing, and keeps a folding chair on the stoop for whoever needs to talk. Loyal to the tenants, allergic to the landlord's lawyer.
catchphrases: The boiler's older than me and nicer than the landlord. Facts.
You want to know who lives in 3R? Ask who's been taking out the recycling.
dislikes: Anybody who says "luxury" about a walk-up

profiles.name: Bernadette "Bernie" Szabo
profiles.background: Hungarian-American, born in Astoria to a family of union printers
profiles.personality: Has run volunteers for every campaign on Steinway since 1994, for whoever pays the rent on the storefront. Loyal to the envelopes, not the candidates.
catchphrases: Grab a stack. Lick, fold, seal. Democracy is mostly envelopes.
Four candidates, one window. I tape up whoever pays this month.
The whiteboard stays facing the wall. I don't care whose campaign you run.

roommates.name: Priya Raman
roommates.background: Indian-American, grew up in Edison, New Jersey, moved to Astoria for nursing school
roommates.personality: Night-shift ER nurse at St. Copay's. Warm, blunt, allergic to dishes left in the sink. Will defend New Jersey to the death.
intro: Hey! I'm Priya, your roommate. I work nights at St. Copay's, so if you hear the door at 7 a.m., that's me, not a burglar.
Rent's split down the middle: your half is {rent}, due {day} every week. The landlord is grimy, but the radiator works. Mostly.
Bathroom schedule's on the fridge. And yes, I'm from Jersey. We can fight about the Statue of Liberty later.
notes: Left you half a pastrami sandwich from Hersh's. The good half. You're welcome.
The radiator is making the noise again. Deadass, it sounds like a trombone.
Night shift was wild. A man came in with a bagel stuck on his thumb. He's fine. The bagel isn't.
Took your umbrella. It's raining in Jersey. Don't ask why I was in Jersey.
Rent day's coming. Leave your half on the fridge like a civilized person.
Also Sal says hi. Also Sal is a cat. I've been awake for 20 hours.
Bought the good dish soap. That's a love language. Use it.
roommates.lola: Your roommate's sweet till {day}. That's when rent's due. Deadass.
